purpose: Test whether measurable engineering-task characteristics explain meaningful variation in independently verified autonomous-agent outcomes, strongly enough to support future delegation decisions. This is a capability-signal experiment, not a concurrency experiment and not an economic one.
northStarQuestion: Do task characteristics provide stable, decision-relevant signal about which engineering work is suitable for autonomous delegation?
whyConcurrencyResearchWasPaused: The concurrency programme produced rigorous measurement infrastructure but increasingly predictable results and no decision consumer. REAL_WORK_SCALING_SIGNAL_OBSERVED confirmed that two workers finish faster than one, which queueing theory already implies, while PREDICTION_NO_INCREMENTAL_VALUE showed the interesting version of the question failed. This workstream redirects the same instrument at a decision teams actually face repeatedly: which work to delegate.

baseline.note: origin/main was unchanged at the known head. This branch stacks on the unmerged research/real-work-external-validity-v1 lineage (draft PR #8) because it reuses that workstream's semver-derived fixture and closes the formatter risk that workstream discovered.

benchmark.design: fully crossed: 3 repositories x 5 task classes x 1 task per cell = 15 tasks

configuration.executionStructure: Three separate runner invocations, one per repository, because a run materializes worktrees from a single --repo at a single base revision. Each invocation is workers=1, repetitions=3 over that repository's 5 tasks, giving 15 logical runs per repository and 45 in total. Acceptance, not throughput, is the primary measurement, so splitting by repository does not affect the comparison; trial wall-clock times are per-repository and are not pooled.

modelSelection.constraint: OpenCode only. Codex must not be executed and must not consume quota. No paid provider experiment was authorized, so selection was restricted to free-tier OpenCode models.
modelSelection.reason: Availability re-verified by standalone probe immediately before freezing (cost 0, structured token usage). The same model was used by opencode-capacity-curve and real-work-external-validity-v1, so provider surface stays comparable with prior evidence. No pre-freeze capability probing was done against this corpus: outcome variation across tasks is the measurement, so probing it first would contaminate the result.

knownFeatureLimitations: acceptanceCriteriaType is collinear with taskClass in this corpus: every task of a class shares one criteria type, so the two cannot be separated.
editableFileCount is 1 for all 15 tasks and expectedChangeBreadth is single_file for all 15, so neither varies and neither can be evaluated.
specificationClarity, verificationCostClass and reversibility vary but are partly determined by class.
These limitations are recorded before execution. They are corpus-design constraints, not findings, and must not be presented as results.

signalCriterion.baseline: overall corpus acceptance rate with no task information
positive: At least two pre-registered task classes or structural buckets differ from the corpus-wide acceptance rate by >= 20 percentage points.
The direction is consistent across at least 2 of 3 repetitions.
The effect is not explained solely by provider or infrastructure failures.
Within-class results are not dominated by a single task instance.
signalCriterion.note: Fixed before execution. If corpus construction makes this threshold inappropriate, the issue is recorded and the evidence classified inconclusive rather than the threshold being changed.

prohibitedConclusions: Instance-level prediction of whether a given future ticket will succeed.
Generalization across all repositories, models or agents.
Any claim that a router, scheduler or predictor is justified.
intendedCommand: for repo in version-core glob-matcher-core cli-command-core; do node apps/cli/dist/index.js benchmark-materialize --manifest benchmarks/delegation-v0/manifest.json --repository $repo --destination <checkout>/$repo --tasks-output <tasks>/$repo.json; done && node apps/cli/dist/index.js run --repo <checkout>/<repo> --tasks <tasks>/<repo>.json --workers 1 --repetitions 3 --seed 20260823 --agent opencode --agent-model opencode/hy3-free --order repetition-major --output experiments/task-delegation-signal-v0/<repo>
